summary.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43% YoY to INR469 crore with EBITDA margin of 30% and reported PAT of INR101 crore, helped by a negative tax rate.
summary.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA for the fourth successive quarter, with revenue of INR469 crore (up 43% YoY), gross margin of 71%, and EBITDA of INR139 crore (30% margin). Reported PAT of INR101 crore (up 115%) was flattered by a negative tax rate from reversal of deferred tax liability as the company moves to the new tax regime; the tax rate is guided to normalise to about 25%. Credit rating was upgraded from A+ to AA-, and ROCE improved to 12.5% from 8.8% in FY25. Management declined to give numerical guidance, repeatedly pointing to pipeline launches in FY27 and FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Slight dip YoY, attributed to higher raw material prices

financial_highlights.metric: Operating PBT (before JV share and exceptionals)

financial_highlights.change: +115% YoY; boosted by negative tax rate from deferred tax liability reversal

financial_highlights.value: 12.5% blended (FY26 per call), adjusted ROCE excluding Biologics and NBE 18.3%

segments.name: API (incl. CDMO and polymer)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR260 crore, up 15% YoY; third-party non-captive API sales also grew about 15%. Growth from newly expanded capacity and captive demand from formulations; specialty CDMO saw new developed-market client wins.

segments.name: Formulation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR198 crore, up over 100% YoY; excluding licensing income, base business grew about 112%, driven by US complex portfolio, with EU and ROW support.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR52 crore, up 42% YoY, driven by licensing and partnership deals and CDMO business. Management expects significantly higher growth off a small base.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given; management said growth trajectory looks robust with faster profitability growth and better ROCE across the business.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in a similar ~30% range; management wants to be conservative and over-deliver.
Tax rate expected to normalise to around 25% in coming quarters.
Peptide manufacturing capacity (solid-phase synthesis, start to end) to complete commissioning by end FY27.
Three CDMO NCE programs in advanced phases to commercialise in FY28; about 3 late-stage programs to enter commercialisation next year.
15 new oncology generic product validations on track for FY27.
Three near-term formulation filings (Abraxane, Enzalutamide, Abiraterone) and Rotigotine patch on track for FY28 launch.
Aflibercept biosimilar launch in India in FY27; Nivolumab biosimilar India launch in FY28.
Nor-UDCA global Phase II studies to start in FY27.
No significant capex expected for Biologics or Albumin for at least the next 3 years; API and some formulation molecules continue to receive investment.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR114 crore, funded by internal accruals.
Peptide capacity in India, solid-phase synthesis, commissioning by end FY27.
Management says large Biologics and Formulation capacity is under-utilised; API is highly utilised and receives the incremental capex.
Albumin: Phase I completed, Phase III starting globally; partnered in Europe.
No segment-wise utilisation figures given; IR to follow up.
demand_pricing: Nor-UDCA (NCE, launched in India last year): management says early clinical outcomes are good and order visibility for FY27 is strong; product-level sales not disclosed. Domestic formulation sales dipped QoQ, which management attributed to stocking and manufacturing timing.
Europe formulation sales fell from about INR77 crore to INR57 crore; management attributed this to quarter-to-quarter tender supply variation.
US sales about INR45 crore; management says all US products are complex, not me-too generics.
Pricing: partial pass-through of raw material cost increases; gross margin dipped on higher raw material prices.
CDMO: more than 20 customers across the group; only one CDMO product currently commercial.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR59 crore domestic formulation revenue over two quarters came from Nor-UDCA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-level sales, citing strong order trajectory instead.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic revenue dip QoQ in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to stocking and manufacturing and delivery timing differences, not a demand issue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross margin sustainable, and what was the ex-licensing gross margin last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give product-level margins; the dip was from higher raw material prices, partly passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax strategy and impact of moving to the new regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is switching to the new regime, losing MAT credit (about 25% of tax used) and some R&D-related timing benefits; normal rate expected at about 25%, with the new regime lowering the effective rate by about 9.75 points, partly offset by MAT utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for licensing income and its margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Licensing income is well above the R&D spend behind it, but failed programs are expensed; management said licensing is not recurring like CDMO and depends on continued portfolio development.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company acquire a US manufacturing unit given the proposed 100% tariff on generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is small (US sales about INR45 crore, no me-too generics) and it is evaluating US manufacturing once tariff terms are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add capacity or capex for Biologics and Albumin?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capex is expected for Biologics or Albumin for at least 3 years; capex continues in API and some formulation molecules.

risks_watch: Regulatory risk: management flagged that US FDA views could slow growth; Unicycive OLC received a CRL and is planning to refile in Q3.
Quarter-to-quarter lumpiness in Nor-UDCA domestic and Europe tender volumes.
Gross margin pressure from raw material costs; partial pass-through only.
Tax normalisation to about 25% will lower reported PAT from the Q1 level.
US tariff policy on generic imports and possible broader tariffs; the Biosecurity Act was judged to have no major impact.
Licensing income is lumpy and not guaranteed; some programs will fail and the failures hit the P&L.
Limited disclosure: product-level, client, and segment ROCE details withheld, which limits model building.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the growth and returns story, but evasive on specifics: repeatedly declined product-level sales, margins, and customer detail, and gave no numerical guidance. Management was most open on the capex cycle (no major new capex in Biologics or Albumin for three years) and the tax change.
